title: Phasing in a raised straight-tip catheter order on the Continence Original Medicare Program
content:
When a prescriber raises the quantity on a straight-tip intermittent catheter (A4351) order, a refill on the Continence Original Medicare Program of the Urology and Continence Supply Program phases the increase in. It does so by limiting how many of the refill's 30-day blocks the order's excess counts for.

## Clause

- The previous refill is the program's straight-tip refill with the latest ship date. The earlier order is the written order behind the authorization grant that the previous refill drew on. When the program has no earlier straight-tip refill, there is no earlier order.
- The newest written order is the straight-tip order with the latest order date.

| The program has an earlier order, and the newest order asks more per 30 days than it | The newest order's date, counted back in calendar days from the ship date | The order's excess for the refill counts for |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no more than 60 days | 1 of the 30-day blocks, instead of all of them |
| yes | more than 60 but no more than 180 days | 2 of them |
| yes | more than 180 days | the blocks of the tier's standard supply days: 3 on this tier, whose standard supply is 90 days |
| no: there is no earlier order, or the newest order asks the same or less | any | the blocks of the tier's standard supply days: 3 |

In every case the order's excess counts for no more than the refill's 30-day blocks.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical; earlier order 190, newest order 250 per 30 days, refill of 3 blocks)

| Newest order dated before the ship date | Blocks the excess counts for |
|---|---|
| 60 days | 1 |
| 61 days | 2 |
| 180 days | 2 |
| 181 days | 3 |

For a refill of only 2 blocks, the third row's 3 blocks is held to the refill's 2.
